label: conj:psd-trace-orthogonality
title: PSD-vs-trace orthogonality of canonical atom-braid Wedderburn blocks. At q₀, the partitions λ ⊢ 3A that dominate the Markov trace `Σ_λ y_λ χ^λ(T_w)` and the partitions that dominate the PSD obstruction `α* = 1/(1 − ε_min)` live in *disjoint shape-class subcategories*: trace-dominant = 1/2-row long-string partitions, PSD-dominant = 3+row multi-step narrow partitions. Empirically supported with 10⁵ magnitude separation at A=4 and 10⁹ at A=6.
html:
Conjecture (PSD-vs-trace orthogonality). Decompose H_{3A}(q) into Wedderburn blocks. The partitions maximising the Hecke Markov-trace weight |y_\lambda(q_0)| are 1- or 2-row long-string partitions. The partitions minimising the PSD-cone scaling eigenvalue are 3+row multi-step tall-narrow partitions. No partition belongs to both classes.

The two objectives of the operator-selection problem—maximising the Markov trace and minimising the PSD scaling penalty—pull the solution toward disjoint sectors of the Young lattice. The tension forces the optimal knot operator into compromise Wedderburn channels.
heading: Conjecture
